snip.t: Well-differentiated liposarcoma: looks almost identical to lipoma under the microscope, but is malignant — the only way to tell them apart is a genetic test showing MDM2/CDK4 gene amplification (region 12q13-15)

snip.t: Common surgical lumps include breast lumps, thyroid swellings, hernias, lipomas, abscesses, and lymphadenopathy.

Differentials of a groin swelling: femoral hernia, saphenous varix, inguinal lymphadenopathy, a psoas abscess or bursa, undescended or ectopic testis, a hydrocele of the cord (or in women the canal of Nuck), lipoma of the cord, femoral aneurysm, and a testicular tumour.

qs.e: Lipoma is a benign tumor of mesenchymal origin, specifically from adipose (fat) tissue, following the nomenclature rule of adding -oma to the cell of origin.
